A.claim: Both /benefits routes still carry the admin check after the sign-in check, in the right order, so the earlier fix that keeps regular users out of the benefits page is still in place.
A non-admin who reaches an admin-only route is redirected to /login instead of getting a 403; an earlier report judged this overstated and it was not looked at again.

The /allocations/:userId handler takes the user id from the URL and the route only checks that some session exists, so any signed-in user can read any other user's allocation percentages and full name by stepping through the sequential ids.
The /memos page shows every memo to every signed-in user, but memos store no owner and the page is a shared board, so no per-user data is exposed.
/tutorial and its sub-pages are reachable without sign-in, but they render fixed templates chosen from a fixed list with no session or database data, so nothing user-specific is exposed.
The /profile handlers read and write using the user id from the session only, and no request field names a user, so a user cannot read or change another user's profile.
The /contributions handlers read and write using the user id from the session only, and no request field names a user, so a user cannot read or change another user's contributions.
The admin middleware does not let a request through when the user lookup fails; every non-admin path, including a failed lookup, redirects to /login.

Login sets the user id on the existing session without regenerating the session id (signup does regenerate it), which may allow session fixation, but whether it can be exploited depends on a cookie-planting route and cookie scope that are not in the repository, so it was left open.
The profile update reads body fields by name, so a user cannot set isAdmin through extra body fields.
/dashboard uses the session user id only and showed no access-control defect.
The / route uses the session user id only and showed no access-control defect.
/logout was examined and showed no access-control defect.
GET /learn redirects to a URL taken from the request, an open redirect passed on for later input-handling work without a decision.
GET /research builds an outbound server-side request from query parameters, passed on for later input-handling work without a decision.

The allocations threshold value is inserted into a $where query string, an injection that also returns rows of all users and is not stopped by fixing the URL user id problem; passed on for later work without a decision.
The contributions handler runs eval on request body values, passed on for later input-handling work without a decision.
Memo content is rendered as markdown through marked on the memos page, passed on for later input-handling work without a decision.

B.claim: Both /benefits routes require sign-in and admin, no other route uses the benefits data access, and the profile update cannot set benefitStartDate, so the earlier /benefits fix has no bypass; live requests showed a regular user redirected to /login on GET and POST and the admin served.
A non-admin who reaches an admin-only route is redirected instead of getting a 403; an earlier report judged this informational and it was not raised again.

The /allocations/:userId handler takes the user id from the URL and the route only checks that a session exists, so any signed-in user, and anyone through open signup, can read every other user's allocation percentages and full name by walking the ids, as shown with live requests.

The allocations threshold query value is placed raw inside a $where string, so a signed-in user requesting their own page with a crafted threshold receives every user's allocations and names, and fixing the URL user id alone does not stop it.
A JSON login body with operator objects can select a user record, but the password is compared with strict equality, so login cannot be bypassed this way; tried live.
Signup builds the user document from six named fields and takes _id from a counter, so a signup request cannot set isAdmin or choose its _id; tried live.

The profile update builds its $set from seven named fields and filters on the session user id, so extra keys such as _id, userId, isAdmin or benefitStartDate cannot change another user's record or grant admin; tried live.
Both contributions handlers take the user id from the session, so a userId in the body cannot write another user's contributions; tried live.

Every signed-in user can read every memo, but memos have no owner or recipient and the page is a shared board, so there is no per-user boundary to break; the owner is asked whether memos should be private.
GET / is mounted without the sign-in middleware, but its handler redirects to /login when the session has no user, which gives the same protection.
Signup checks the username and then inserts in a separate step, so two new records can end up with the same name, but no account takeover or privilege gain follows.
The admin middleware calls next only when the stored user record has isAdmin; a database error or a missing user leads to a redirect.
The contributions handler runs eval on request body fields on a route any signed-in user can reach, which reads as server-side code execution; passed on for later work without being checked.
The login lookup uses a request value directly as a query filter, so operator objects from the JSON parser reach the query; passed on for later work without being checked.
The research route builds a URL from query parameters and fetches it server-side; passed on for later work without being checked.
The /learn route redirects to req.query.url; passed on for later work without being checked.
The profile handler applies a backtracking regular expression to bankRouting; passed on for later work without being checked.
Login does not regenerate the session; passed on for later authentication and session work without being checked.
Login returns different messages for an unknown user and for a wrong password; passed on for later work without being checked.
Passwords are stored as received; passed on for later work without being checked.
The session middleware is set up without cookie options such as httpOnly and secure; passed on for later work without being checked.
The CSRF middleware is commented out; passed on for later work without being checked.
The session secret is fixed in configuration with no environment override; passed on for later work without being checked.
Template autoescaping is turned off; passed on for later work without being checked.
Memo markdown is rendered without escaping; passed on for later work without being checked.
The allocations view writes the URL path parameter into the form action, a source that the URL user id fix would remove; passed on for later work without being checked.
The SSN, and the date of birth, are stored in clear; passed on for later work without being checked.
The tutorial pages are static teaching content, public by design and reachable without sign-in, so their views were not read.
/login, /signup, /logout, static assets and the favicon are reachable without sign-in.
/dashboard, /profile, /contributions, /allocations/:userId, /memos, /learn and /research all require sign-in through the isLoggedIn middleware.
Every signed-in route other than /allocations/:userId takes the record id from the session or has no per-user record, so those routes keep users to their own data.
The sign-in middleware calls next only when the server-side session holds a user, and the user is set only after the password check or after signup.
An admin using the regular-user routes sees only the admin's own records.
Case variants, trailing-slash variants and HEAD requests go through the same middleware chain as the normal routes.
The static file mount serves only app/assets.
